Q: why is my Neural Network stuck at high loss value after the first epochs A:

As your loss decreases from 40000 to 6000, that means your NN model has learnt the prevalent relation but not all of them. You can aid this learning by transforming the predictor variables and then feeding them as derived ones to your model and see if that helps. You can try performing step wise addition of features to your NN model, by adding the most influential predictors first. At every iteration evaluate the model performance (i.e. training loss).

If first step doesn't help and as you are open to other approaches, Presuming your data's dynamics, Gaussian process Regression or Quantile regression should help as these methods are free from assumptions like linear regression techniques. Also it should help to explore different aspects of relationship between your independent and dependent variable.

Q: Using parallel computing to fit multiple models A:

For the parallel version, foreach + doParallel is the most straightforward drop-in:

library(foreach)
library(doParallel)

cl <- makeCluster(parallel::detectCores() - 1)
registerDoParallel(cl)

results <- foreach(
  i = seq_len(n_combos),
  .packages = "forecast",
  .errorhandling = "pass"
) %dopar% {
  cols <- which(grid[i, ] == TRUE)
  xreg_train <- x[, cols, drop = FALSE]

  tryCatch({
    fit <- auto.arima(y, xreg = xreg_train)
    xreg_future <- matrix(rep(xreg_train[n, ], each = h),
                          nrow = h,
                          dimnames = list(NULL, colnames(xreg_train)))
    fc <- forecast(fit, xreg = xreg_future, h = h)
    list(vars = names(grid)[cols], aicc = fit$aicc,
         bic = fit$bic, model = fit, fc = fc)
  }, error = function(e) {
    list(vars = names(grid)[cols], error = conditionMessage(e))
  })
}

stopCluster(cl)

future.apply::future_lapply with plan(multisession) is an equally valid alternative if you prefer that ecosystem.

That said, I'd echo Roland's comment: exhaustive subset selection across 511 models and then picking the best AICc isn't well-calibrated, since AICc doesn't account for the search process itself. Regularization (e.g. LASSO/elastic net on the regressors with ARIMA errors) or at minimum model averaging via MuMIn::dredge() would be more defensible approaches.
